messages:
Carla M.: quick check — customer asked how to fully opt out of client telemetry (no user-agent augmentation, no metrics, no traces). what’s the canonical approach for the node and python SDKs?
Ben R.: for node we expose an env var and a config flag. env is REDWOOD_CLIENT_TELEMETRY=false. config: { telemetry: { enabled: false } } — should that also suppress the UA header?
Ally K.: it should. when telemetry is disabled we must stop sending any non-required headers (UA, app-id, client-metrics). otherwise customers worried about leakage.
Carla M.: ok good. can someone paste the minimal example for both languages so i can send to support?
Dan S.: node example:
```
// new SDK
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, telemetry: { enabled: false } });
await client.text.generate({ model: 'redwood/fast-1', input: 'hi' });
```
or env-only: `REDWOOD_CLIENT_TELEMETRY=false` (process env read at init).
Priya N.: python example:
```
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key=os.environ['RW_KEY'], telemetry={'enabled': False})
c.text.generate(model='redwood/fast-1', input='hi')
```
or export REDWOOD_CLIENT_TELEMETRY=false before starting app.
devex-bot: note added: docs/telemetry/opt-out (draft) created by @Dan S. — /docs link: https://redwood.internal/docs/telemetry/opt-out
Ben R.: small nuance: tracing propagation headers (traceparent) — if telemetry is off we should not inject auto-generated trace ids. however if customer supplies their own tracing headers we should preserve/passthrough them to downstream model endpoints (so their trace stays intact).
Ally K.: agreed — semantics: when telemetry.enabled=false -> stop creating new spans/ids and stop adding UA+client metrics. BUT do not strip existing inbound tracing headers. just pass-through.
Carla M.: good point. need to clarify in docs: "disable telemetry" vs "strip incoming headers".
Dan S.: also saw a weird race in streaming clients: when telemetry is disabled the streaming connection still emits a startup metric from the runtime on connection open — that comes from the serving layer. we should ensure the client runtime omits any non-required handshake fields when telemetry is disabled. filed an infra ticket.
Priya N.: PR #2314 in the SDK repo implements env var + config. i left a TODO about user-agent format when enabled (we still want a compact UA like `redwood-sdk/{lang}@{version}` not full os details).
Ben R.: QA checklist suggestion:
- unit test that REDWOOD_CLIENT_TELEMETRY=false results in no UA header
- e2e that inbound traceparent gets forwarded unchanged
- streaming smoke test to validate no handshake metric emitted
- docs snippet for both languages and env var example
Carla M.: can someone drop the exact header names we use for tracing so support can search logs?
Ally K.: we follow W3C `traceparent` and `tracestate`. additionally we have a legacy header `x-rw-trace-id` that some partners still use — we forward both if present.
Dan S.: note for maintainers: avoid removing trace headers on the client when telemetry disabled. only stop adding `x-rw-client-metrics` and `x-rw-user-agent` and the SDK-generated `trace-id` header.
Priya N.: pinging @Ben R. for code review on PR #2314, should land today if no objections.
Ben R.: i'll review now, will merge if green. :eyes:
Carla M.: thanks everyone — i'll update the support playbook with the two examples and the clarifications about pass-through vs strip. cc @devex-bot for doc link when merged. :thumbsup:
devex-bot: PR #2314 merged into main by @Ben R. — docs link: https://redwood.internal/docs/telemetry/opt-out (published draft)
